claims: Vaccines stimulate the immune system to produce antibodies.
Vaccines stimulate the body’s immune system to create an imitation infection.
The imitation infection is a mild form of the actual disease.
The imitation infection does not cause the disease itself.
Vaccination teaches the immune system to recognize and fight the pathogen.
Vaccination enables the immune system to combat the real disease upon future exposure.
The body develops T lymphocytes and B lymphocytes that remember how to fight the infection.
Routine vaccines include Tdap, flu, and MMR.
Immunization protects against or reduces the severity of influenza, tetanus, measles, polio, and COVID-19.
Childhood immunizations include DTaP (diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis), Hib, polio, MMR (measles, mumps, rubella), and chickenpox.
Adult vaccines include annual flu shot, Tdap, shingles, and RSV.
Common minor side effects of immunizations include fever or soreness.
Immunizations can cause soreness or swelling at the injection site.
Pharmacies like Walgreens and medical offices offer routine vaccines
